text.p: Following are the main stories from Austrian newspapers on Thursday.
DIE PRESSE
- Harsher punishment for child sex abuse and longer prison terms are envisaged in the wake of the latest child porn ring scandal in the Salzburg region.
- Salzburg Festival organiser Gerard Mortier attacks regional conservative official who wants more "public-friendly" programmes.
- Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel does not want to bring party squabbles over his position as conservative People's Party leader into the public spotlight.
- Jehovas witnesses are going to take their case to the highest court to try to win recognition as a religious society.
DER STANDARD
- Steyr Daimler Puch vehicle parts maker will in future supply parts to British Rover group and Korean Hyundai.
- The Vienna Social Democrats support current President Thomas Klestil as their preferred candidate for the presidential elections in the autumn.
- The Spanish Riding School will this year celebrate its 425th anniversary.

- Economy ministry wants to tighten the reins of major oil companies in price regulation. "We don't want to go back to price regulation but a slight (price) decline on a voluntary basis under liberalisation," a government official said.
- Globalisation trend is continuing full steam ahead, says OECD's latest report. This year could be the most ground-breaking in terms of firm takeovers.
- Stock market jitters are increasing daily. After weeks of rallies, any sign of inflation pressures triggers big losses.
KURIER
- Police believe the so-called Bajuwarische Befreiungs Armee, which claims responsibility for a spate of racially motivated letterbombs, tried out their bombs several times before sending them.
- A secret paper of the Vienna police shows a dramatic rise in violent crime in the last 10 years since the opening up of the former Eastern bloc.
- Women's Minister Barbara Prammer wants to introduce a preference system for public companies that promote women.
- Steelmaker VA Stahl wants to expand its interests in Poland.
- Luxury hosiery maker Wolford has postponed its New York Stock Exchange debut to March 1998.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank is ploughing on with expansion plans in central and eastern Europe. The next target is Bucharest.
- Oil and chemicals group OMV has the go-ahead from its supervisory board for partnership talks with Finnish plastics producer Borealis.
- Big discounts have fuelled shopping enthusiasm this year but turnover was down in the first half overall.
